questions.text: No single crop or product gave more than 70 percent of our sales income last year.
anchors: One crop or product gave over 90 percent of sales
One crop or product gave 71 to 90 percent of sales
One crop or product gave 51 to 70 percent of sales
Largest crop or product gave 36 to 50 percent of sales
Largest crop or product gave 35 percent or less of sales

evidence.requirement: Sales records or invoices by crop or product for the last 12 months, to work out the largest share.

questions.text: We have a written business plan with targets and a budget for the next 1 to 3 years, and we reviewed it in the last 12 months.
anchors: No written plan of any kind
Only a verbal plan or a list of ideas
Written plan with targets but no budget, not reviewed in 12 months
Written plan with targets and budget, reviewed once in 12 months
Plan with targets and budget, reviewed at least twice with changes noted and shared with members or staff

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the plan and the dated review notes or minutes.

questions.text: Before each season we check which crop or product has a ready buyer and a positive margin, and we choose what to plant, process or stock on that basis.
anchors: We plant or stock what we did last year without checking
We choose by what neighbours plant or what seed is available
We ask one buyer or trader informally, with nothing written
We compare at least two crops or products using buyer prices and our own costs
We have a written crop or product comparison with buyer commitments before planting or stocking

evidence.requirement: Ask how the last crop choice was made and look for notes, buyer quotes or a margin comparison.

questions.text: We have a written agreement (offtake, supply or purchase) with at least one buyer, covering volume, price basis and quality.
anchors: No agreement, we sell to whoever pays on the day
Verbal understanding with a buyer only
A written order or note for one delivery, missing price basis or quality
Written agreement covering volume, price basis and quality for the current season
Signed agreement covering volume, price basis, quality and payment terms, honoured by both sides last season

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the signed agreement or purchase order and compare it with last season deliveries.
examples: Purchase order from processor or institution

questions.text: In the last 12 months we delivered at least 95 percent of the volume our buyers ordered, on the agreed dates.
anchors: Delivered under 50 percent of ordered volume on time, or lost a buyer for failure to deliver
Delivered 50 to 69 percent on time
Delivered 70 to 84 percent on time
Delivered 85 to 94 percent on time
Delivered 95 percent or more on time, shown by delivery notes

evidence.requirement: Compare orders with delivery notes or goods received notes for the last 12 months.

questions.text: No single buyer took more than half of our sales last year.
anchors: One buyer took over 90 percent of sales
One buyer took 71 to 90 percent of sales
One buyer took 51 to 70 percent of sales
Largest buyer took 31 to 50 percent of sales
Largest buyer took 30 percent or less, and we have at least three active buyers

evidence.requirement: Sales records by buyer for the last 12 months.

questions.text: Our buyers paid us on the agreed date for most deliveries in the last season.
anchors: Buyers paid on the agreed date for under 25 percent of deliveries
Paid on time for 25 to 49 percent of deliveries
Paid on time for 50 to 74 percent of deliveries
Paid on time for 75 to 89 percent of deliveries
Paid on time for 90 percent or more, and we follow up late payments in writing

evidence.requirement: Compare invoice dates, agreed payment dates and receipt dates for last season.

questions.text: Before agreeing a selling price, we check current prices from at least two sources, such as markets, buyers, aggregators or a price information service.
anchors: Never, we accept the first price offered
Rarely, only when a neighbour tells us
Sometimes, from one source
Usually, from at least two sources, but not recorded
Always from at least two sources, with prices written down before we agree

evidence.requirement: Ask when the last price was agreed and look for the price notes or messages used.

questions.text: We have a plan for when to sell, such as selling in stages or storing for a better price, and we did not sell all our produce at the harvest glut last season.
anchors: We sold all produce straight after harvest at the lowest price
We sold most produce at harvest because we needed cash, with no plan
We sold some later, but only by chance
We planned to sell in at least two stages and followed the plan for most produce
Written selling plan tied to cash needs and storage, followed, with sales dates and prices recorded

evidence.requirement: Look at sales dates and prices through the season and any selling plan.

questions.riskTag: All produce sold at harvest glut

questions.text: We sell part of our produce after cleaning, grading, shelling, drying or processing, so that we earn more than the raw farm-gate price.
anchors: We sell everything raw and ungraded
We clean or grade sometimes but sell at the same price as raw
We clean or grade most produce and sometimes get a better price
We clean, grade or process more than half of our produce and get a better price from at least one buyer
We sell graded or processed produce under a price premium shown in sales records

evidence.requirement: Compare prices for graded or processed lots with raw lots in sales records.

questions.riskTag: No value captured above raw price

questions.text: We check every lot we buy or collect for moisture and for foreign or damaged material before we accept it.
anchors: Never, we accept produce by sight
Rarely, only when a buyer complains
Sometimes, for some suppliers
Usually, with a meter or standard test, but results not recorded
Always for every lot, with results recorded and poor lots rejected or graded

evidence.requirement: Observe an intake or ask to see the intake record and the moisture meter or test tools.

questions.text: We can show a buyer where each lot came from (member or farm, village and date of purchase).
anchors: We cannot say where any lot came from
We can name the source for some lots, from memory or loose notes
Every lot has a written source (member or farm, village, date) that we can show a buyer within a day

evidence.requirement: Pick three recent lots and ask for their source records.

questions.text: Our last delivery to our main buyer passed the buyer's quality check without rejection or price cut.
anchors: Last delivery was rejected, or we do not know the buyer's requirements
Delivery was accepted only with a price cut for quality
Delivery was accepted but we hold no written quality requirement from the buyer
Delivery passed and we hold the buyer's written quality or certification requirements
Delivery passed, we hold the written requirements, and we check our lots against them before dispatch

evidence.requirement: Ask for the buyer's written requirements and the last quality or rejection report.

questions.text: We write a plan before each season showing area per crop, expected yield, and the inputs, labour and money we will need.
anchors: No plan, we decide as the rains start
Plan kept in our heads only
Written plan for area and inputs, without yield or labour
Written plan covering area, expected yield, inputs and labour
Written plan covering all four, with costs, approved by the leaders or owner, and compared with results after harvest

evidence.requirement: Ask for this season's plan and last season's comparison of plan against actual.

questions.text: We know our own average yield per acre for our main crop over the last 3 seasons, from records and not from guesswork.
anchors: We do not know our yield per acre
We give a rough guess, with no records
We know last season's yield from records for our main crop
We know yields for the last 2 seasons from records
We hold yield per acre records for 3 seasons, by plot or group, and can explain changes

evidence.requirement: Ask for harvest records and area measures, then recompute yield per acre.

questions.text: Most of the area we plant each season uses certified or improved seed of varieties suited to our rainfall, bought from a registered seller.
anchors: None of our area uses certified or improved seed
Under 25 percent of area uses certified or improved seed
25 to 49 percent of area uses certified or improved seed
50 to 79 percent of area uses certified or improved seed
80 percent or more of area uses certified or improved seed, with receipts and variety names kept

evidence.requirement: Check seed receipts, bag labels and the area planted against the plan.
examples: Seed bag labels with lot number

questions.text: For our main crop we follow the planting time, spacing and fertiliser rate advised by extension or the seed or fertiliser supplier, and we can show what we did.
anchors: We follow no advice and keep no record of what we apply
We follow advice for some practices but do not know the recommended rates
We know the advised practices and follow some of them
We follow most advised practices on most of the area and keep field notes
We follow advised practices on nearly all the area, record each operation, and an extension officer has visited this season

evidence.requirement: Ask for field notes and visit a plot, or ask an extension officer or lead farmer to confirm.

questions.text: We receive the seed, fertiliser and chemicals we need before planting time in most seasons, without delays that cost us yield.
anchors: Never on time, planting is often late for lack of inputs
Rarely on time
Sometimes on time
Usually on time, with a small delay in some seasons
Always on time, ordered ahead with a written order and delivery date

evidence.requirement: Compare input delivery dates with planting dates for the last two seasons.

questions.text: We buy inputs from known registered suppliers and compare prices or terms from at least two before we buy.
anchors: Never, we buy from whoever is nearby
Rarely compare, and suppliers are not registered
Sometimes compare
Usually compare at least two suppliers, using registered dealers
Always compare at least two registered suppliers, with quotes kept

evidence.requirement: Ask for the last input purchase and the quotes or messages used to compare suppliers.

questions.text: We record who received which inputs from us, how much, and what each person still owes.
anchors: No record of inputs given out
Some names noted in a notebook, without amounts owed
Names and quantities recorded, amounts owed not tracked
Names, quantities and amounts owed recorded for all recipients
Complete ledger updated at each issue and repayment, balanced against stock and checked by a second person

evidence.requirement: Sample five recipients and match issue records with repayment records.

questions.applies: Supplies inputs on credit to members, outgrowers or customers only

questions.text: We buy sealed, labelled seed, fertiliser and chemicals from licensed sellers, and we check the label and expiry date before use or resale.
anchors: We use or sell repacked or unlabelled inputs, or do not check expiry
We buy from market traders and rarely check labels
We check labels or expiry on some purchases
We buy from licensed sellers and check label and expiry on most purchases
We buy only sealed, labelled inputs from licensed sellers, check every pack, and keep receipts and batch numbers

evidence.requirement: Inspect the input store and a sample of packs, and ask for purchase receipts.

questions.text: We dry and clean produce to the buyer's or national moisture standard before storing or selling, and we measure moisture to confirm.
anchors: We store or sell produce without drying to a standard
We dry by sight on the ground and never measure moisture
We dry on tarpaulins or a drying floor, and measure moisture sometimes
We dry on tarpaulins or a drying floor and measure moisture on most lots
We dry on clean surfaces or a dryer, measure moisture on every lot, and record readings before storage

evidence.requirement: Observe drying and look for moisture records on lots going into store.

questions.text: Our store is clean, dry and off the ground with a written pest control routine that we follow.
anchors: Produce is stored on the floor or in a leaking or dirty place
Store is roughly clean but produce touches walls or floor, no pest routine
Store is clean and dry with produce on pallets, pest control done only when pests appear
Store is clean, dry, on pallets, with a pest routine followed but not recorded
Store clean, dry and on pallets, with a written routine and dated pest control records, checked by an inspector or buyer

evidence.requirement: Visit the store and ask for the pest control routine and records.

questions.text: We have measured how much produce we lost after harvest in the last season and can name the main causes.
anchors: We have never thought about post-harvest loss
We say there is loss but have no figure
We have a rough estimate for one crop, without causes
We measured loss for our main crop and named at least two causes
We measured loss at each step (drying, storage, transport) for our main crops and acted on the biggest cause

evidence.requirement: Ask for the loss figures and what was changed in response.

questions.text: We rotate stock first in, first out, and the oldest lots are sold or processed before newer ones.
anchors: Never, newest stock is taken first or old stock is forgotten
Rarely
Sometimes, when we remember
Usually, and old stock is marked
Always, with dated lots stacked so the oldest is reached first and checked monthly

evidence.requirement: Walk the store and check dates on lots against what has been sold.

questions.text: We keep a business bank account or business mobile money wallet separate from personal or household money, and business money passes through it.
anchors: No separate account, business and personal money are mixed
Separate account exists but is mostly unused
Separate account used for some receipts or payments
Separate account used for most receipts and payments, with some personal use
All business receipts and payments go through the separate account, with no personal use seen in statements

evidence.requirement: Review three months of statements for the business account or wallet.

questions.text: We write every sale and every expense in a cash book, notebook or app within one week of it happening.
anchors: Never, we rely on memory
Rarely, only large transactions
Sometimes, but with gaps of more than a month
Usually within a week, with occasional gaps
Always within a week, with receipts or mobile money messages attached

evidence.requirement: Take five transactions from bank or mobile money statements and find them in the book.

questions.text: We can show written records of sales, costs and loan repayments for the last 2 to 3 seasons.
anchors: No records for any past season
Records for part of the last season only
Complete records for the last season only
Complete records for the last 2 seasons
Complete records for the last 3 seasons, summarised by season

evidence.requirement: Ask for season summaries and trace two entries to source documents.

questions.text: At any time we can say how much buyers or members owe us, and how much we owe suppliers and lenders, from written lists.
anchors: We do not know what we are owed or what we owe
We know roughly from memory
We keep a list of what we are owed but not of what we owe
We keep lists of both, updated at least monthly
Both lists are updated weekly, dated, and agree with the cash book

evidence.requirement: Ask for the lists as of today and check two items against receipts.

questions.text: We prepare a month-by-month cash plan across the season showing when money will come in and go out.
anchors: No cash plan
Verbal idea of when money is needed
Written list of big costs, without months for income
Written monthly cash plan for the season covering income and costs
Monthly plan updated at least quarterly against actual cash, and used to decide borrowing and selling

evidence.requirement: Ask for the current season cash plan and the last update.
examples: Cash flow plan spreadsheet or notebook page

questions.text: We know how much money we need before harvest (for weeding, labour, hired services and household needs) and where it will come from.
anchors: We do not know and borrow when we run short
We know roughly but have no source lined up
We know the amount and have a possible source, not confirmed
We know the amount and have a confirmed source, such as savings, a loan or a buyer advance
We know the amount, have confirmed funding, and a back-up source, written in the cash plan

evidence.requirement: Ask for the pre-harvest budget and evidence of the funding source.

questions.text: We keep a cash or savings reserve that could cover at least one month of running costs in the lean season.
anchors: No reserve at all
Reserve covers under 1 week of running costs
Reserve covers 1 to 3 weeks of running costs
Reserve covers 4 to 7 weeks of running costs
Reserve covers 8 weeks or more of running costs, held in a safe account

evidence.requirement: Compare the balance on the statement or passbook with monthly running costs.

questions.riskTag: No cash reserve for lean season

questions.text: At least once each season we compare our cash plan with actual cash in and out, and change our plan when the two differ.
anchors: Never, there is no plan to compare
Once in several seasons
Once a season, without changing the plan
Twice a season, with the plan changed after one comparison
At least quarterly, with a written note of the changes made

evidence.requirement: Look for the dated comparison and the revised plan.

questions.text: We have recorded the full cost of production per acre for our main crop in the last season, including labour, inputs and hired services.
anchors: We have never worked out our cost of production
We have a rough guess with no records
We counted inputs only, not labour or services
We counted inputs, hired labour and services for our main crop
We counted all costs, including family labour valued at a local rate, for each main crop, from records

evidence.requirement: Ask for the cost sheet and trace three costs to receipts.

questions.text: We know the profit per acre, or per bag, kg or litre, for each of our main crops or products from last season.
anchors: We do not know whether we made a profit on any crop
We feel we profited, with no figures
We know profit for one crop or product from rough figures
We know profit for each main crop or product using records
We know profit for each main crop or product and compared them to choose what to expand or drop

evidence.requirement: Ask for the margin calculation and compare revenue and cost records.
examples: Sales and cost records by crop

questions.text: We know our break-even price per bag or kg, and we do not sell below it unless the leaders or owner decide so.
anchors: We do not know our break-even price
We guess a minimum price with no calculation
We calculated break-even once, but do not use it when selling
We calculated break-even this season and use it as a minimum in most sales
Break-even is updated each season, written, and every sale below it is approved and recorded

evidence.requirement: Ask for the break-even figure and sales below it in the last season.

questions.text: An independent person (an auditor, accountant or trained reviewer who is not the book-keeper) checks our accounts at least once a year.
anchors: Nobody outside the book-keeper ever checks our books
Informal check by a leader or friend, with nothing written
Independent check done once in the last 2 years, with a written note
Independent check each year with a written report
Annual audit or review by a qualified accountant, report shared with members or lenders, and findings acted on

evidence.requirement: Ask for the latest review or audit report and action list.

questions.text: The person who receives cash is not the same person who records it or who approves large payments.
anchors: One person receives, records and approves cash and payments
Two people are involved in some transactions only
Receiving, recording and approving are done by different people, with approval signatures on payments above a set limit

evidence.requirement: Observe a cash receipt and a payment, and look for signatures on payment vouchers.

questions.text: In the last 3 years we repaid every loan (bank, microfinance, input credit or group loan) in full and by the due date, shown by lender records.
anchors: We defaulted, or have an overdue unpaid loan today
We repaid most loans late, or had loans rescheduled twice or more
We have never borrowed, so there is no repayment record
We repaid all loans, but at least one was more than a month late
We repaid every loan in full by the due date, confirmed by lender or group records

evidence.requirement: Ask for lender statements or letters, repayment schedules and receipts.

questions.text: Repayment dates on any loan match when we get paid, such as after harvest sales, and not before.
anchors: Repayments fall before harvest with no income to meet them
Repayments are monthly with no link to our income dates
Some repayments follow harvest and some do not
Most repayments follow the months when we are paid
Repayment dates were set from our cash plan, or we have no loan and know the timing we would need

evidence.requirement: Compare the repayment schedule with the cash plan and sales dates.

questions.riskTag: Repayment dates do not match income

questions.text: Money we borrow is used for what we said it was for, and we keep receipts showing how loan money was spent.
anchors: Loan money was used for other purposes with no record
Part of loan money went to household spending, with no record
We used the loan for the stated purpose, but kept few receipts
We used the loan for the stated purpose and have receipts for most spending
All loan spending is matched to the plan with receipts and a short report to the lender or group

evidence.requirement: Compare the loan application purpose with receipts and cash book entries.

questions.text: Our yearly loan repayments take less than a third of our yearly net income in a normal season.
anchors: Repayments take over 60 percent of net income
Repayments take 46 to 60 percent of net income
Repayments take 34 to 45 percent of net income
Repayments take 20 to 33 percent of net income
Repayments take under 20 percent of net income, or we have no loans and can show net income

evidence.requirement: Compute repayments over net income from season summaries and repayment schedules.

questions.text: Our savings group or cooperative savings follow written rules on shares, loans, interest and fines, and the rules are linked to the group's farming or business activity.
anchors: No written rules for savings or loans
Verbal rules only, applied unevenly
Written rules exist, but are not followed on loan size or repayment
Written rules followed for savings and loans, and passbooks are up to date
Written constitution followed, all transactions in front of the group with passbooks and ledger, and a yearly share-out

evidence.requirement: Ask for the constitution, ledger and passbooks and attend or ask about a meeting.

questions.text: We have used at least two different sources of finance in the last 2 years, such as a bank, microfinance, VSLA, supplier credit, buyer advance or asset finance.
anchors: No outside finance used and none available to us
Used one source only, on informal terms
Used one formal or group source
Used two different sources
Used three or more sources and compared terms before choosing

evidence.requirement: Ask for evidence of each source used and the terms compared.

questions.text: We know the terms of any input credit, buyer advance or outgrower deal we take, including interest or price deduction, and these are written down.
anchors: We take advances or input credit with no written terms
We know the terms in outline only, nothing written
Terms written, but we do not know the total cost to us
Terms written and we can say the total cost of the credit in cedis or bags
Terms written, total cost worked out, and compared with a bank or other option before we agreed

evidence.requirement: Ask for the credit or advance agreement and the cost calculation.

questions.text: We have used or checked a warehouse receipt, asset finance or lease option for equipment or storage, and we know the requirements to qualify.
anchors: We do not know of any such options
We have heard of them but have not checked requirements
We have asked about one option and know part of the requirements
We know the requirements of at least one option and have a plan to meet them
We have used one option, or applied, with documents prepared

evidence.requirement: Ask for application papers, quotes or notes on requirements.

questions.text: We prepare yearly financial statements (income statement, balance sheet and cash flow) that a lender or investor could read.
anchors: No financial statements prepared
A list of sales and costs only
Income statement only, prepared for one year
Income statement and balance sheet for the last year, prepared from records
Income statement, balance sheet and cash flow for the last 2 years, reviewed or audited

evidence.requirement: Ask for the latest statements and check they agree with the cash book.

questions.text: We hold a written list of our assets (land, equipment, buildings, stock) with their approximate value and who owns each.
anchors: No list of assets
Verbal list only
Written list without values or owners
Written list with values and owners for most assets
Written register with values, owners, condition and documents (receipts, site plan), updated yearly

evidence.requirement: Ask for the asset register and see two items.

questions.text: We hold documents that a lender would accept as security, such as land documents, warehouse receipts, stock records or a buyer contract assignment.
anchors: We hold no document a lender could use
We hold documents that are in someone else's name or are disputed
We hold one acceptable document of small value
We hold acceptable documents covering part of a typical loan
We hold acceptable documents covering a typical seasonal loan, checked by a lender or advisor

evidence.requirement: Ask for the documents and a lender or advisor view if available.

questions.text: We have a written funding request showing how much we need, what it will buy, how it will earn money, and when it will be repaid.
anchors: No written funding request
Written note with the amount only
Written request with amount and use, no repayment plan
Written request with amount, use and expected return, with simple figures
Funding request with budget, cash flow, repayment plan and supporting records, shown to a lender or partner

evidence.requirement: Ask for the latest funding request or application.

questions.text: If the owner, manager or chairperson is away for two weeks, another named person can run buying, selling and payments using written instructions.
anchors: Nothing works when the main person is away
Someone helps informally, but cannot access money or contracts
A named deputy exists, but has no written instructions or access
A named deputy has written instructions and can approve routine payments
Deputy tested during an absence in the last 12 months, with written instructions and signing rights

evidence.requirement: Ask who deputised last time and look for written instructions and signing rights.

questions.text: Our owner, manager or leaders completed training in business, farm or group management in the last 2 years, and we can show it.
anchors: No training in the last 2 years
Attended one short event, with no certificate or notes
Attended training and can describe what was learned
Attended training and used at least one new practice, shown in records
Attended training and use several new practices, with a plan for further training of leaders

evidence.requirement: Ask for certificates, attendance lists or training notes and one example of change made.

questions.text: We have a written plan for who leads or owns the enterprise or group if the current leader leaves, falls ill or dies.
anchors: No plan, and nobody has discussed it
Plan discussed but not written down
Written plan naming successors or a process, known to the board, family or members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the written plan and who knows about it.

questions.text: Our members elect leaders at a general meeting, and each member has one vote.
anchors: Leaders were never elected, or are appointed by one person
Leaders were elected more than 4 years ago and not since
Leaders elected in the last 4 years, but voting was by show of a few people
Leaders elected at a general meeting with most members voting, one member one vote
Elections held on schedule in by-laws, with voter list, minutes and results shown to members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the election minutes, attendance list and by-laws.

questions.text: Most members attend our general meetings, and each year they receive a report on money, sales and decisions.
anchors: No general meeting held in the last 2 years
General meeting held but under a third of members attended, no report given
A meeting held in the last year, with a verbal report only
Meeting held in the last year with over half of members and a written or read-out annual report
Yearly meeting with over two thirds of members and a written report on accounts, sales and decisions, with questions recorded

evidence.requirement: Ask for the meeting minutes, attendance list and last annual report.

questions.text: Most members sell most of their crop through the group, and we know how much they sold elsewhere.
anchors: Members sell under 10 percent of their crop through the group, or we do not know
Members sell 10 to 24 percent through the group
Members sell 25 to 49 percent through the group
Members sell 50 to 74 percent through the group, measured for at least half of members
Members sell 75 percent or more through the group, measured from member records

evidence.requirement: Compare group purchase records with member production estimates for last season.

questions.text: The roles of owner or board, managers and staff or members, and who can approve spending and sign contracts, are written down and followed.
anchors: Roles and approval powers are not written
Roles are known verbally, with no approval limits
Roles are written, but approval powers are unclear
Roles and approval limits are written and mostly followed
Roles, approval limits and signing powers are written, signed, followed and reviewed yearly

evidence.requirement: Ask for job descriptions, by-laws or an approval policy and check one recent contract or payment.

questions.text: No child below 15 works in our enterprise or on our farm, and no one under 18 does hazardous work such as spraying chemicals or carrying heavy loads.
anchors: Children below 15 work regularly on our farm or enterprise, or do hazardous work
Children help during school time or do hazardous tasks sometimes
Children help only outside school hours on light tasks, with no policy
We have a rule against child labour and children do not do hazardous tasks, but we do not check
Written rule, ages checked for all workers and suppliers, school attendance protected, and issues recorded and fixed

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the rule, worker ages and what is done when a child is found working.

questions.text: In the last 12 months our staff, members or workers received training in a skill we need, such as good farming practice, storage or record keeping, with an attendance list.
anchors: No training in the last 12 months
Informal advice only
One training session with an attendance list
Two or more sessions covering different skills, with attendance lists
A yearly training plan based on gaps, delivered, attendance recorded and results checked

evidence.requirement: Ask for the training plan, attendance lists and examples of skills used afterwards.

questions.text: An extension officer, agronomist or technical adviser visited our farms or members at least once in the last season, and we recorded the advice.
anchors: Never visited
Rarely visited, advice not recorded
Visited once, advice recorded
Visited at least twice with advice recorded
Visited regularly (about monthly in the season) with advice recorded and applied

evidence.requirement: Look for visit notes, officer names and what changed after visits.

questions.text: Members or outgrowers who take group inputs or credit repay on time, and we keep a record of who owes what.
anchors: Under 50 percent of credit was repaid on time, or no record is kept
50 to 69 percent repaid on time, records incomplete
70 to 84 percent repaid on time, records complete
85 to 94 percent repaid on time, records complete
95 percent or more repaid on time, from a complete signed ledger

evidence.requirement: Compare the ledger of credit given with repayments received last season.

questions.text: We pay the farmers, members or suppliers who sell to us on the date we promised, and they receive a payment slip or message.
anchors: Under 50 percent of payments are on the promised date
50 to 69 percent on the promised date
70 to 84 percent on the promised date
85 to 94 percent on the promised date
95 percent or more on the promised date, with slips or messages kept

evidence.requirement: Compare promised dates, payment dates and slips for three suppliers.

questions.text: Members, outgrowers, workers and suppliers have a known way to raise a complaint, and we record and answer complaints.
anchors: No way to complain
Complaints are heard informally, with no record
A person is named for complaints, but nothing is recorded
Complaints are recorded and most are answered within a month
Known channel (box, phone, committee), all complaints recorded, answered and reported to leaders or members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the complaints log and one case history.

questions.text: We keep a register of the farms or plots we farm or buy from, showing the owner, crop, area in acres and where the plot is.
anchors: No register of farms or plots
A list of names only
Register with names and crops, no areas or location
Register with names, crops, area and village or landmark for most plots
Register with names, crops, measured area and GPS point or sketch map for nearly all plots, updated each season

evidence.requirement: Ask for the register and check three plots against it.

questions.text: We keep batch and stock records that show what came in, what went out and what is in the store, updated each time stock moves.
anchors: No stock records
Stock counted occasionally, nothing written
Stock book written, but updated only weekly or monthly
Stock book updated at each movement, with batch numbers on most lots
Stock cards by batch updated at each movement, counted monthly and matched to the book

evidence.requirement: Do a physical count of one product and compare with the stock record.

questions.text: We give a receipt or delivery note for every sale or purchase, and keep a copy.
anchors: Never
Rarely, only if asked
Sometimes, for large transactions
Usually, for most transactions with copies kept
Always, numbered, with copies filed and matched to the cash book

evidence.requirement: Check three recent transactions for numbered receipts or notes with copies.

questions.text: We keep important records (contracts, receipts, member lists, accounts) for at least 2 years in a safe place, with a copy kept elsewhere.
anchors: Records are lost, scattered or kept for less than a year
Records are kept loosely at home or in the store
Records are filed in one place, with no copy
Records are filed in one safe place and key items are copied or photographed
Records are filed, copied or backed up off site, and we can find any item from the last 2 years in a day

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the file store and retrieve a record from last season.

questions.text: We use mobile money or bank transfers to pay farmers and workers, and to receive payment from buyers, for most of our transactions.
anchors: Almost all transactions are in cash (under 10 percent digital)
10 to 29 percent of transactions are digital
30 to 59 percent of transactions are digital
60 to 89 percent of transactions are digital
90 percent or more of transactions are digital, with statements kept

evidence.requirement: Compare cash and digital payments over a month of records.

questions.text: We keep our records on a phone app, spreadsheet or computer system, with backups, and not only on paper.
anchors: No digital records
Photos of paper records only
One spreadsheet or app used for one record type
Spreadsheet or app used for sales, stock and costs, backed up occasionally
Spreadsheet or app used for all core records, backed up weekly, with named person responsible

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the app or spreadsheet and the last backup.

questions.text: Each month we compare our mobile money or bank statement with our own records and explain any difference.
anchors: Never
Rarely, only when something is missing
Sometimes, but we do not explain differences
Usually monthly, with differences noted
Every month, differences explained and signed by a second person

evidence.requirement: Look for a reconciliation sheet for the last three months.

questions.text: Passwords, PINs and signing rights for our accounts and wallets are held only by authorised people and are not shared informally.
anchors: PINs and passwords are shared widely or written openly
Several informal users share one wallet or login
Authorised users are known, but one login is shared
Each authorised person has own login and PIN, with some informal sharing seen
Each authorised person has own login and PIN, access is reviewed when roles change, and no sharing is observed

evidence.requirement: Ask who can access each account and check the signatory list.

questions.text: Leaders or owners review sales, costs, stock and loan balances at least monthly in a meeting or written note.
anchors: Never
Once or twice a year
Quarterly
Monthly, but without written notes
Monthly with written notes and actions followed up

evidence.requirement: Look for the last three review notes or minutes.

questions.text: We track at least five measures with targets, such as yield per acre, cost per bag, deliveries on time, repayment rate and post-harvest loss.
anchors: We track none
We track one or two measures with no targets
We track three or four measures, targets for some
We track five or more measures with targets, reviewed each season
We track five or more measures with targets and trends over 3 seasons, shown to leaders or members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the scorecard or dashboard and the last season values.

questions.text: We collect data from our members, outgrowers or suppliers each season (area, expected and actual output, inputs received) and use it to plan.
anchors: No data collected
Data from a few leaders only
Data from half of members or suppliers, not used for planning
Data from most members or suppliers and used for planning volumes
Data from nearly all members or suppliers, checked on a sample, and used to plan purchases, inputs and finance

evidence.requirement: Ask for the last season data sheets and the plan that used them.

questions.text: Last season's results changed something we did this season, and we can name the change and the result that led to it.
anchors: Nothing changed, and results were not discussed
We talked about results, but changed nothing
We changed one thing without linking to records
We changed one thing and can link it to a recorded result
We changed several things, linked to records, and we tracked whether the change worked

evidence.requirement: Ask for an example and the record that led to the change.

questions.text: Our business, farm group or cooperative is legally registered with the right body (Registrar General or Department of Cooperatives) and the registration is current.
anchors: Not registered
Registration started but not completed
Registered, but certificate or annual returns are out of date
Registered, certificate current, annual returns filed in the last year
Registered, certificate current, returns filed, and by-laws or regulations on file and followed

evidence.requirement: Ask for the registration certificate and the latest annual return or audit letter.

questions.text: We have a Tax Identification Number and we filed the tax returns that apply to us on time in the last year.
anchors: No TIN and no returns filed
TIN held, but no returns filed in the last year
Returns filed late or incomplete
Returns filed on time for the last year
Returns filed on time for the last 2 years with proof of filing and any payments

evidence.requirement: Ask for the TIN certificate and filing acknowledgements.

questions.riskTag: Tax filings not up to date

questions.text: We hold written proof of our right to use the land we farm or store on (lease, allocation letter, customary grant record or title), covering at least the next 3 years.
anchors: No proof of right to use the land
Verbal permission only
Written note from the owner without witnesses or dates
Written agreement with the owner or traditional authority covering the next 3 years
Registered or witnessed document covering at least the crop cycle or tree life, held by the enterprise

evidence.requirement: Ask for the land documents and check the signatories and dates.

questions.text: We know whether our farming or processing activity qualifies for a tax incentive, and we have claimed what applies to us.
anchors: We do not know of any tax incentive
We have heard of incentives but have not checked if we qualify
We checked and qualify, but have not claimed
We checked and claimed one incentive that applies
We checked all that apply, claimed them, and hold proof from the tax authority or our tax adviser

evidence.requirement: Ask for the tax advice, claim or approval letter.

questions.text: We hold the current registrations, licences and permits that our activity needs from the agencies that regulate us (for example FDA, EPA, PPRSD, TCDA or Department of Cooperatives).
anchors: We hold none and do not know which apply
We know some apply but hold none
We hold some, and know of gaps
We hold all we need, current
We hold all we need, current, with a renewal calendar kept and followed

evidence.requirement: Ask for a list of applicable regulators and each certificate or licence with expiry dates.

questions.text: We hold a TCDA export permit and proof of payment of the development levy before each export shipment of raw shea or cashew.
anchors: We export raw shea or cashew without a permit
We have applied for a permit but have not received it
We hold a permit but have no levy proof for shipments
We hold a permit and levy proof for most shipments
We hold a current permit and levy proof for every shipment, filed with phytosanitary papers

evidence.requirement: Ask for the TCDA permit, levy receipts and the file for the last shipment.

questions.applies: Exports raw shea or cashew only

questions.text: Our store or processing site and the food products we sell meet FDA requirements for what we do (licence, premises, labelling and records).
anchors: No FDA licence or inspection, and we do not know the requirements
We know the requirements but meet few of them
We meet some requirements, with open gaps from an inspection or checklist
We meet most requirements and hold a valid licence
We meet all requirements, hold a valid licence, and have no open inspection findings

evidence.requirement: Review the FDA licence and the last inspection report, and visit the premises.

questions.text: We are certified, or following a written plan with dates to be certified, for the standard our target markets require (for example organic, Fairtrade, GlobalG.A.P. or the Global Shea Alliance programme).
anchors: No certification and no knowledge of what markets require
We know the standard but have no plan
We have started preparation, with no dates
We have a written plan with dates and a budget, and have done a gap check
We hold a current certificate or approved status, and passed the last audit

evidence.requirement: Ask for the certificate, audit report or the written plan and gap check.

questions.riskTag: Not certified or planning to be

questions.text: At least once a year we check our own practices against the standard or buyer rules we follow, and fix what we find.
anchors: Never, we do not check
Only when a buyer or auditor visits
Once in the last 2 years
Yearly, with findings listed
Yearly, with findings listed, fixed by a date and checked

evidence.requirement: Look for the self-assessment checklist and the corrective actions.

questions.text: We use only registered pesticides, applied by trained people wearing protective gear, and we record what was applied, where and when.
anchors: Unregistered or banned chemicals are used, or no protection and no records
Registered chemicals mostly, but no protective gear or records
Registered chemicals and some protective gear, no records
Registered chemicals, trained sprayers with protective gear, records kept for most applications
Registered chemicals only, trained sprayers, protective gear, empty containers handled safely, and complete records

evidence.requirement: Inspect the chemical store, sprayer equipment and the application record.

questions.text: We have a written list of the main risks to our enterprise (weather, price, theft, buyer default, illness) with at least one action for each.
anchors: No list of risks
Risks discussed verbally
Written list of risks without actions
Written list with an action for most risks
Written list with actions, owners and dates, reviewed each season

evidence.requirement: Ask for the risk list and a recent update.

questions.text: We have insurance on at least one major risk to our crop, livestock, stock or equipment, and we know what the policy covers.
anchors: No insurance and no knowledge of options
We know of options but have none
Insurance on one asset, but we cannot say what it covers
Insurance on our main crop, livestock or stock, with cover known
Insurance on our main risks, with premium budgeted, policy on file, and a claim process known

evidence.requirement: Ask for the policy, premium receipt and cover summary.

questions.text: Before we sell on credit or give inputs on credit to a new customer or member, we check their record and set a credit limit in writing.
anchors: We give credit to anyone who asks
We give credit to people we know, with no limits
We set limits for some customers, not written
We check record and set written limits for most customers
We check record, set written limits, and review overdue accounts monthly

evidence.requirement: Ask for the credit policy and the aged debtors list.

questions.text: We have a written plan with at least two actions for a dry spell, flood or pest outbreak, such as early maturing seed, staggered planting or a second income.
anchors: No plan for any weather or pest shock
We talk about shocks but have no plan
Plan for one shock only, with one action
Plan covering two or three shocks with at least two actions each
Written plan with actions, owners and costs, tested or used in the last 3 seasons

evidence.requirement: Ask for the plan and an example of when it was last used.
examples: Seed purchase for early maturing varieties

questions.text: Each season we obtain the seasonal rainfall forecast or weather advisory (for example from the Ghana Meteorological Agency or a radio or phone service) and use it to time planting and other work.
anchors: Never use any forecast
Rarely, only if we hear it by chance
Sometimes, but we do not change our plans
Usually receive it and have changed timing at least once
Always receive it before planting, record how it changed our timing, and share it with members or staff

evidence.requirement: Ask for the forecast received and an example of changed planting or spraying dates.

questions.text: Last season we spread risk by planting on staggered dates, or by planting drought or heat tolerant varieties on part of our area.
anchors: No staggering and no tolerant varieties
Under 10 percent of area used one of these methods
10 to 24 percent of area used one of these methods
25 to 49 percent of area used one of these methods
50 percent or more of area used one or both of these methods, shown in the season plan

evidence.requirement: Check the planting dates by plot and seed receipts or variety names.

questions.text: We keep a record of weather and pest shocks (dry spells, floods, outbreaks) and their cost to us in each of the last 3 seasons.
anchors: No record of any shocks
Verbal memory of shocks, with no figures
Written notes for the last season, with no cost
Written record with cost for the last season
Written record with dates and cost for the last 3 seasons

evidence.requirement: Ask for the record and compare with yield or loss records.

questions.text: We have a plan to look after our land, trees and water, for example tree planting, soil care and no bush burning, and we followed it last season.
anchors: No plan, and bush burning or tree cutting without replanting is common
Informal intention only
Written plan covering one area (trees, soil or water)
Written plan covering trees, soil and water, followed in part
Written plan with targets, followed and counted (trees planted, plots under soil care, fire breaks)

evidence.requirement: Ask for the plan, then visit a plot or tree site to check.

questions.riskTag: No land and water care plan

questions.text: On most of our area we use practices that keep soil fertile, such as legume rotation, manure or compost, crop residue cover or contour ridges.
anchors: No soil care practice on any area
Practices on under 10 percent of area
Practices on 10 to 29 percent of area
Practices on 30 to 59 percent of area
Practices on 60 percent or more of area, recorded in the season plan or field notes

evidence.requirement: Check field notes and visit two plots to see the practice.

questions.text: Our farm, processing site or store holds the EPA registration or permit that its size and activity require, or EPA has confirmed in writing that none is needed.
anchors: We do not know whether we need an EPA registration or permit
We know it may apply but have not applied
We applied and are waiting, with receipts
We hold the registration or permit required
We hold the permit, meet its conditions, and keep the compliance records

evidence.requirement: Ask for the permit or EPA letter and compare the size of operation with EPA thresholds.

questions.text: We dispose of waste from our farm or site (empty chemical containers, processing waste, plastic) safely, away from water sources and food.
anchors: Waste is dumped or burned near water, food or homes
Waste is left in the open and empty chemical containers are reused
Waste is gathered in one place but not safely disposed
Waste is separated, and empty chemical containers are punctured and stored away from food
Waste is separated, safely disposed or reused, with a written routine and a named person

evidence.requirement: Visit the waste area and ask how containers and processing waste are handled.

questions.text: Women who farm with us, supply us or work for us take part in decisions and have a say in how money from sales is used.
anchors: Women are not asked, and men decide how sales money is used
Women are asked occasionally, but men decide
Women speak in meetings, but do not influence how sales money is used
Women take part in decisions and influence some spending of sales money
Women take part in decisions and share control over use of sales money, shown in minutes or reports

evidence.requirement: Ask women members or staff directly, and review minutes or payment records.

questions.text: Women who farm with us can own or use the land, trees, tools and equipment they need through our group or enterprise, in their own name or jointly.
anchors: Women have no access to land, trees or equipment through us
Women can use assets only through male relatives
Women can use some assets, with no written rights
Women have written use rights to some assets
Women have written rights in own name or jointly to land, trees or equipment, with examples checked

evidence.requirement: Ask women members to describe their access and check lease, share or allocation records.

questions.text: Women hold leadership roles or sit on committees, and at least one third of leaders or managers are women.
anchors: No women in any leadership role
Women hold under 10 percent of leadership roles
Women hold 10 to 24 percent of leadership roles
Women hold 25 to 33 percent of leadership roles
Women hold more than one third of leadership roles, including at least one office-bearer post

evidence.requirement: Count leaders and committee members from the current list.

questions.text: Young people (aged 18 to 35) have defined roles or paid work with us, such as in production, aggregation, processing or records, and we know how many.
anchors: No young people involved
A few young people help informally, unpaid
Young people have some paid work, but we have no count
We can count the young people in paid or defined roles
We count young people by role, they take part in decisions or training, and we track their numbers each season

evidence.requirement: Ask for the list of young workers or members and their roles.
examples: Staff or member list with ages

subDimensions.name: Enterprise strategy and crop or product portfolio

mapping.gapPattern: Enterprise grows whatever it grew last year, depends on one crop, and has no written plan beyond the next planting.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise is exposed to one crop and one season, and has no written direction that a lender, buyer or partner can assess.
mapping.prescription: Before the next land preparation (March to April in the north), write a one to three year plan with a crop or product margin comparison, and add a second income line such as a processed product or a legume rotation crop.

intervention.resources: Business plan template, crop margin comparison sheet, three coaching sessions before planting

measurement.kpi: Share of sales from the largest crop or product
measurement.baselineMethod: Sales records by crop for the last 12 months
measurement.provisionalTarget: Largest crop under 70 percent of sales, written plan approved

mapping.gapPattern: Selling to whoever pays on the day, verbal buyer promises, late or short deliveries and one dominant buyer.
mapping.diagnosis: Sales are not secured by contract, so deliveries, prices and payment dates are unpredictable and cannot support input credit.
mapping.prescription: Negotiate a written offtake or supply agreement with at least one buyer before planting (April to June), with volume, price basis, quality and payment date, and agree a delivery calendar the enterprise can meet.

intervention.resources: Buyer introductions (processors, institutional buyers, aggregators), model offtake agreement, legal review

measurement.kpi: Written buyer agreements in force and on-time delivery rate
measurement.baselineMethod: Contract file and delivery notes for last season
measurement.provisionalTarget: At least one signed agreement and 90 percent on-time delivery

subDimensions.name: Pricing, market information and value capture

mapping.gapPattern: Price taken from the first offer, all produce sold at the harvest glut, and no grading or processing to earn more.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise captures the lowest price in the year because it sells unprepared, unpriced produce at the point of greatest supply.
mapping.prescription: Collect prices from at least two sources every week of the marketing season (October to March), set a minimum price from break-even, and plan staged sales with cleaning and grading so part of the crop is sold after the glut.

intervention.resources: Weekly price tracker, selling plan template, grading guide, access to price information service

measurement.kpi: Average price received compared with the seasonal average price
measurement.baselineMethod: Price notes and sales records for last marketing season
measurement.provisionalTarget: Average price at or above the seasonal mean, two or more sales tranches

mapping.gapPattern: Produce is bought or collected without testing, lots cannot be traced to a farm or village, and buyer rejections are common.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise cannot prove quality or origin, so it is excluded from quality-linked and institutional markets and loses premiums.
mapping.prescription: Before the buying season starts (September to October), install intake testing with a calibrated moisture meter, a lot register that records farm or member, village and date, and adopt the written specification of the main buyer.

intervention.resources: Moisture meters, lot register template, intake grading training, buyer specification review

measurement.kpi: Share of lots with an intake test and a traced source
measurement.baselineMethod: Sample of 20 lots at the start of the buying season
measurement.provisionalTarget: 95 percent of lots tested and traced, rejection rate falling
measurement.dataSource: Intake book, lot register, buyer quality reports

mapping.gapPattern: No written plan per season, yield per acre unknown, late planting and local seed with unrecorded practices.
mapping.diagnosis: Production is run by habit, so the enterprise cannot forecast volumes, cost inputs or show lenders and buyers a credible yield.
mapping.prescription: Before planting (April to June), prepare a season plan per plot with area, expected yield, inputs and labour, use certified or improved seed and advised practices, and record harvest per plot to calculate yield per acre.

intervention.resources: Season plan template, harvest record book, extension officer visits, demonstration plot

measurement.kpi: Average yield per acre for the main crop compared with district average
measurement.baselineMethod: Harvest records for last three seasons, or farmer recall with sampling
measurement.provisionalTarget: Yield per acre recorded for all main plots, 10 percent improvement against baseline

mapping.gapPattern: Inputs arrive after the first rains, there is one supplier, input credit is untracked and packs are unlabelled or repacked.
mapping.diagnosis: Late, untested or untracked inputs lower yield and create credit losses that break the link with members and lenders.
mapping.prescription: Order inputs by March for the main season, compare at least two licensed suppliers, buy only sealed labelled packs, and keep an input ledger of every issue and repayment.

intervention.resources: Input order calendar, supplier comparison sheet, input ledger template, list of licensed dealers

measurement.kpi: Share of inputs received before planting date, and input credit recovery rate
measurement.baselineMethod: Delivery notes and ledger from last season
measurement.provisionalTarget: 90 percent of inputs on time, input ledger complete

mapping.gapPattern: Produce stored wet or on the floor, no moisture reading, no pest routine, stock rotated by chance and losses unmeasured.
mapping.diagnosis: Post-harvest handling is losing quantity and quality and creating aflatoxin and rejection risk, especially for maize and groundnut.
mapping.prescription: Before harvest (August to September), set a drying standard with a moisture meter, upgrade the store with pallets and hermetic or triple bags, adopt a written pest routine and FIFO, and measure loss over one storage season.

intervention.resources: Moisture meters, tarpaulins or dryer plan, hermetic bags, store checklist, loss measurement sheet

measurement.kpi: Post-harvest loss percentage and share of lots stored below the moisture standard
measurement.baselineMethod: Stock in and out records and moisture readings at store intake
measurement.provisionalTarget: Loss measured and falling, 100 percent of lots under the standard at intake
measurement.dataSource: Stock cards, moisture log, store inspection

mapping.gapPattern: Business and household money mixed, no cash book, gaps in records and debts unknown.
mapping.diagnosis: Without separate money and written records the enterprise cannot prove income, repay reliably or qualify for credit.
mapping.prescription: Open a business account or mobile money wallet immediately, start a cash book that is written within a week, and rebuild a season summary of sales, costs and repayments for the last two seasons from receipts and statements.

intervention.resources: Cash book or app, account opening support, receipt book, season summary template

measurement.kpi: Share of transactions recorded within one week and months of complete records
measurement.baselineMethod: Review of the last three months of statements against the cash book
measurement.provisionalTarget: 90 percent recorded within a week, two seasons of summaries built

subDimensions.name: Seasonal cash flow and working capital

mapping.gapPattern: No cash plan, money runs out in the lean months (about June to August), pre-harvest costs unfunded and no reserve.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise is exposed to a seasonal cash gap, so it borrows at bad terms or sells early and cheaply.
mapping.prescription: Build a month-by-month cash plan before planting (April), identify the pre-harvest gap and fund it from a reserve, VSLA or buyer advance, and compare plan with actual every quarter.

intervention.resources: Seasonal cash plan template, pre-harvest budget sheet, quarterly review checklist

measurement.kpi: Months of the season with a funded cash plan and reserve in weeks of running costs
measurement.baselineMethod: Interview and review of last season bank or wallet balances
measurement.provisionalTarget: Cash plan complete and updated quarterly, reserve of four weeks

mapping.gapPattern: Cost of production never calculated, profit per crop unknown and sales sometimes below cost.
mapping.diagnosis: Decisions on crops, prices and borrowing are made without knowing margins, so some activities lose money unnoticed.
mapping.prescription: After harvest (November to January) calculate full cost per acre and per bag for each main crop, compute margins, set a break-even minimum price and use it in the next planting decision.

intervention.resources: Cost of production template, margin calculator, break-even sheet

measurement.kpi: Cost per acre and break-even price for each main crop
measurement.baselineMethod: Cost records and receipts for last season
measurement.provisionalTarget: Costs and break-even known for all main crops

mapping.gapPattern: The book-keeper handles all cash, nobody checks the books and the accounts have never been reviewed independently.
mapping.diagnosis: Weak controls leave the enterprise open to loss and fraud and block access to credit that needs reviewed accounts.
mapping.prescription: Separate receiving, recording and approving cash, set approval limits, and commission an independent review of the accounts after the season closes (December to February).

intervention.resources: Cash control checklist, voucher templates, independent reviewer or accountant

measurement.kpi: Independent review completed and number of control gaps open
measurement.provisionalTarget: Annual review done, no high risk gap open

mapping.gapPattern: Late or defaulted loans, repayment dates set without regard to harvest, loan money used for other things and heavy debt burden.
mapping.diagnosis: Repayment problems signal weak cash management and make lenders unwilling to extend seasonal credit.
mapping.prescription: Renegotiate or time new loans so repayment follows harvest sales, use loans only for the purpose in the application with receipts, and cap yearly repayments at about one third of net income.

intervention.resources: Loan timing worksheet, repayment calendar, lender statement review, one lender meeting

measurement.kpi: Repayment on time rate and debt service as a share of net income
measurement.provisionalTarget: All repayments on time, debt service under one third of net income

subDimensions.name: Alternative and group finance (VSLA, outgrower, asset finance)

mapping.gapPattern: One source of finance, group savings without clear rules, credit terms not understood and no use of warehouse receipts or asset finance.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise relies on a single, often expensive source and misses cheaper or group-based finance that fits the season.
mapping.prescription: Map finance options (VSLA, bank, input credit, buyer advance, warehouse receipt), calculate the total cost of each, write savings group rules and adopt the VSLA cycle of weekly meetings and a yearly share-out.

intervention.resources: Finance options map, credit cost calculator, VSLA training manual, introductions to lenders and warehouse operators

measurement.kpi: Number of finance sources used and cost of credit known in cedis
measurement.provisionalTarget: Two or more sources, total cost known for each

mapping.gapPattern: No financial statements, assets unlisted, no acceptable security and no written funding request.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise cannot present itself to a lender or investor, even when it is operationally sound.
mapping.prescription: Prepare income statement, balance sheet and cash flow for the last year, list assets with owners and values, gather security documents, and write a funding request with budget and repayment plan.

intervention.resources: Financial statement templates, asset register, funding request template, mock lender review

measurement.kpi: Investor-ready pack completeness (statements, asset register, security documents, funding request)
measurement.baselineMethod: Checklist against a lender requirements list
measurement.provisionalTarget: Four of four pack items complete

mapping.gapPattern: The owner or chair is the only person who can act, no leader training and no succession plan.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise depends on one person, so illness, absence or exit can stop buying, selling and payments.
mapping.prescription: Name a deputy with written instructions and signing rights, enrol leaders in business management training in the off-season, and write a short succession plan.

intervention.resources: Deputy handover template, leadership training list, succession note template

measurement.kpi: Deputy in place with signing rights and leader training in last two years
measurement.provisionalTarget: Deputy tested once, leaders trained, succession plan on file

mapping.gapPattern: Leaders not elected, meetings rare, members sell outside the group and roles and approval powers are unwritten.
mapping.diagnosis: Member trust and loyalty are weak, so volumes are unreliable and the group cannot honour buyer contracts.
mapping.prescription: Hold a general meeting with elections and a written annual report after harvest (December to February), measure side-selling, write roles and approval limits, and agree member rules on selling through the group.

intervention.resources: By-laws review, meeting templates, annual report template, member loyalty survey

measurement.kpi: Share of members' crop sold through the group and meeting attendance
measurement.baselineMethod: Group purchase records against member production survey
measurement.provisionalTarget: 50 percent sold through the group, over half of members at the yearly meeting

mapping.gapPattern: Child labour risk, no skills training, no extension visits and labour shortages at planting.
mapping.diagnosis: People risks (child labour, unskilled work, no advice) threaten buyer acceptance, certification and productivity.
mapping.prescription: Adopt a child labour rule with age checks before the planting rush (April), train workers and members before the main season, and arrange extension visits during crop growth (June to September).

intervention.resources: Child labour policy and checklist, worker register, training attendance lists, extension officer schedule

measurement.kpi: Child labour incidents found and share of workers or members trained in last 12 months
measurement.provisionalTarget: No incidents, 70 percent trained, two extension visits per season

mapping.gapPattern: Group credit not repaid, farmers paid late, and no way to raise complaints.
mapping.diagnosis: Weak member and supplier relations lead to side-selling, defaults and loss of trust that undermine every contract.
mapping.prescription: Keep a signed credit ledger, pay suppliers on promised dates with slips, and open a complaints channel with a log reviewed by leaders every quarter.

intervention.resources: Credit ledger template, payment slip book, complaints register

measurement.kpi: Credit recovery rate and share of supplier payments on the promised date
measurement.baselineMethod: Ledger and payment records from last season
measurement.provisionalTarget: 90 percent recovery, 90 percent of payments on time, complaints logged

mapping.gapPattern: No plot register, stock or sales records, no receipts and records lost or kept loosely.
mapping.diagnosis: Without records the enterprise cannot trace produce, prove sales or show a track record to buyers and lenders.
mapping.prescription: Set up a plot register, stock cards, a numbered receipt book and a filing routine with photo backup before the buying season (September).

intervention.resources: Plot register, stock card, receipt book, file box and backup routine

measurement.kpi: Core records complete (plots, stock, receipts, filing)
measurement.provisionalTarget: Four of four in use and checked monthly

subDimensions.name: Digital tools, payments and market information

mapping.gapPattern: Mostly cash payments, paper-only records, statements never checked and PINs shared.
mapping.diagnosis: Cash handling and informal access raise fraud and loss risk and leave no digital trail for lenders.
mapping.prescription: Move farmer and worker payments to mobile money, keep records in a simple app or spreadsheet with backup, reconcile monthly, and restrict PIN and signing rights.

intervention.resources: Mobile money merchant set-up, spreadsheet template, monthly reconciliation sheet

measurement.kpi: Share of payments made digitally and months reconciled
measurement.provisionalTarget: 70 percent digital, reconciled every month

mapping.gapPattern: No regular review, no measures with targets, no member data and no learning from results.
mapping.diagnosis: Leaders manage by feel, so problems are seen late and improvements are not tracked.
mapping.prescription: Agree five measures with targets, hold a monthly review of sales, costs, stock and loans, collect member production data at planting, and write one change per season linked to results.

intervention.resources: Scorecard template, monthly review agenda, member data sheet

measurement.kpi: Measures tracked with targets and monthly reviews held
measurement.provisionalTarget: Five measures tracked, 10 reviews held a year

mapping.gapPattern: Not registered, tax filings missing and no proof of land rights.
mapping.diagnosis: Legal and land gaps block contracts, loans, grants and investment and risk eviction from the farm.
mapping.prescription: Complete registration with the Registrar General or Department of Cooperatives, obtain a TIN and file returns, and record customary or leased land rights in writing before planting.

intervention.resources: Registration checklist, tax adviser, Customary Land Secretariat or lawyer, land document templates

measurement.kpi: Registration, tax filing and land documents in order (count of three)
measurement.provisionalTarget: Three of three in place and current

mapping.gapPattern: Licences and permits not held, TCDA export rules not followed, and premises do not meet FDA requirements.
mapping.diagnosis: Regulatory gaps risk seizure, fines and loss of buyers and block certification and export.
mapping.prescription: List every regulator that applies, apply for missing licences before the buying season (August to September), follow TCDA permit and levy rules for raw shea and cashew exports, and fix FDA inspection findings.

intervention.resources: Regulator checklist, FDA and TCDA application support, premises gap check

measurement.kpi: Required licences and permits held and current
measurement.provisionalTarget: All applicable permits current, no open FDA finding

mapping.gapPattern: No certification plan, no internal checks and unsafe pesticide use.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise cannot meet buyer and export compliance requirements and risks rejection for chemical residues.
mapping.prescription: Choose the standard the target buyers need, do a gap check, run an internal inspection each year before harvest, and train sprayers and keep application records.

intervention.resources: Standard gap check, internal inspection checklist, pesticide safety training, application record sheet

measurement.kpi: Gap check completed and open non-conformities against the chosen standard
measurement.provisionalTarget: Plan with dates, internal inspection done, pesticide records for all sprays

mapping.gapPattern: No risk list, no insurance and credit given to customers without limits.
mapping.diagnosis: The enterprise carries all weather, price and credit risk alone, so one bad season can end it.
mapping.prescription: Write a risk list with actions, price and take up crop, livestock or stock insurance before planting (April to June), and set written credit limits for customers.

intervention.resources: Risk register template, insurance quotes from GAIP or other insurers, credit policy template

measurement.kpi: Insured share of main crop value and risks with actions
measurement.provisionalTarget: Main crop or stock insured, risk list with actions

mapping.gapPattern: No plan for dry spells or floods, forecasts unused, planting not staggered and shocks unrecorded.
mapping.diagnosis: Climate variability, strong in northern Ghana, can wipe out a season because the enterprise has no response plan.
mapping.prescription: Write a shock plan with two actions per risk, collect the seasonal forecast before planting (April), stagger planting or use tolerant varieties on part of the area, and record shocks and losses.

intervention.resources: Seasonal forecast access, shock plan template, climate smart practice guide, shock log

measurement.kpi: Share of area using staggering or tolerant varieties and shock plan in place
measurement.provisionalTarget: 25 percent of area, plan in place, forecast used
measurement.dataSource: Season plan, forecast copy, shock log

mapping.gapPattern: No land and water care plan, little soil care, no EPA permit and unsafe waste disposal.
mapping.diagnosis: Soil and environmental neglect lowers future yield and blocks grants, certification and permits.
mapping.prescription: Write a land, trees and water plan, apply soil care on at least 30 percent of the area in the next season, obtain EPA registration or written confirmation, and set a waste routine.

intervention.resources: Land and water plan template, soil care guide, EPA registration support, waste routine

measurement.kpi: Share of area under soil care and EPA status
measurement.provisionalTarget: 30 percent of area under soil care, EPA status confirmed

mapping.gapPattern: Women lack a voice, assets and leadership roles, and young people have no defined roles.
mapping.diagnosis: Exclusion reduces production, loyalty and funding access, since donors and certifiers now check gender and youth inclusion.
mapping.prescription: Set targets for women's participation in decisions and leadership, record women's land and equipment access, and define roles for young people in the next season plan.

intervention.resources: Women's group dialogues, pro-WEAI based checklist, youth roles list, leadership coaching

measurement.kpi: Share of leadership roles held by women and number of young people in defined roles
measurement.provisionalTarget: One third of leaders women, young people counted by role

readiness.name: Input and working capital credit readiness
readiness.purpose: Whether the enterprise can safely take and repay input and working capital credit for the season.
readiness.unlocks: Unlocks: apply for seasonal input credit or a working capital loan, timed for April to June.

readiness.name: Offtake and institutional market readiness
readiness.purpose: Whether the enterprise can supply buyers, processors and institutional markets reliably with quality produce.
readiness.unlocks: Unlocks: bid for an offtake contract or institutional supply with a processor, aggregator or programme.

readiness.name: Certification and export readiness
readiness.purpose: Whether the enterprise could pass a certification or export audit on quality, traceability, safety and legal basics.
readiness.unlocks: Unlocks: start certification (organic, Fairtrade, GlobalG.A.P., Global Shea Alliance programme) or an export permit process.

readiness.name: Investment readiness
readiness.purpose: Whether the enterprise has the records, governance and legal base for an investor or term lender.
readiness.unlocks: Unlocks: approach lenders and investors for equipment, storage or processing capital.

readiness.name: Grant and climate-finance readiness
readiness.purpose: Whether the enterprise can receive and account for grants and climate finance.
readiness.unlocks: Unlocks: apply for grants and climate-smart agriculture funding with inclusion and environmental safeguards in place.

consistencyChecks.rule: Multi-season records are claimed but the habit of writing transactions is absent.
A separate business account is claimed, yet almost all transactions are in cash.
Yield per acre is claimed from records, yet there is no register of plots or areas to compute it.
Lot origin is claimed, yet there is no register of farms or plots to trace to.
Yearly financial statements are claimed, yet there are no multi-season records to build them from.
High sales through the group are claimed, yet no member production data exist to measure them.
